Date: 2026-11-14 | Start: 08:00 PT | Duration: ~42 minutes | Meeting id: ff-20261114-helion-01 | Recording: yes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM); Dr. Maya Rios, Carlos Mendes, Priya Nair, Evan Holt (Helion Health)
summary: Quarterly-ish operational sync focused on reducing per-token and per-request costs while keeping latency SLOs; discussed dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, KV cache benefits on conversational flows, upcoming pilot to validate economic uplift, compliance artifacts requested. Agreed next steps include cost breakdown, dedicated pilot provisioning, and SOC2/network docs. Decision lean: run a dedicated pilot then evaluate commit if 30-40% cost improvement realized.
topics: Usage patterns and tail latency for conversational assistants
Per-model cost allocation and hot routes
Dedicated capacity trial and autoscale/overprovision tradeoffs
KV cache / prefix caching impact on token cost
Compliance artifacts: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, VPC peering
Roadmap alignment: schema for rollout and evaluation criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Dr. Maya Rios: Hi, Maya here — sorry I'm a few minutes late, been in a clinic visit.
[00:09] Carlos Mendes: Carlos on the line.
[00:11] Priya Nair: Priya, Cloud.
[00:13] Evan Holt: Evan, SRE.
[00:15] Samir Patel: Samir Redwood SE.
[00:17] Lina Gomez: Lina Redwood CSM.
[00:20] Avery: Cool. We'll go through ops, cost, reliability, then the roadmap and next steps. We've got about 40ish minutes. Maya, do you want to kick off with a quick status?
[00:28] Dr. Maya Rios: Sure. Overall things have been stable. Throughput's up 12% month-over-month cause of the new triage flow, but cost is creeping; we're seeing a noticeable spike in per-session tokens for longer follow-ups — the assistant tends to keep context and it's adding up.
[00:48] Priya Nair: To add, our finance folks flagged the October bill; they want a forecast model for November if we roll into peak season. So predictability matters.
[00:58] Avery: Understood. On that we recommended a dedicated pool in the past — Samir, remind them the economics there?
[01:06] Samir Patel: Yeah. With Dedicated you get reserved GPU capacity which flattens out the per-token compute charge — effectively you convert a lot of variable cloud spend into a fixed commitment. For Helion's current load, a 3-month reserved plan with a 20% commit gets you better unit costs, but the win is bigger if you can enable aggressive KV cache and batching.
[01:29] Carlos: Sorry, quick Q — the KV cache, does it store whole messages or tokens? We have PHI concerns for some conversation segments.
[01:36] Samir: Good question. It's prefix and KV-based; you can configure what gets cached and what doesn't. Also Redwood supports encryption-at-rest with customer KMS, and you can opt out for segments with PHI. There's a mask-and-tokenize pattern we usually suggest.
[01:50] Dr. Maya Rios: We need to make sure that caching doesn't retain PHI beyond the session. We have strict retention rules. How do you do deletion?
[01:57] Lina Gomez: We have retention policies in Console — you can set TTLs and run purge jobs. Samir can share the exact retention controls and the API for programmatic deletes.
[02:05] Priya: Also network: we need clear diagrams. Our security team needs to know egress endpoints for logs, and whether the control plane touches payloads in Private deployment.
[02:14] Avery: Lina will send the SOC2 plus the network diagram after the call.
[02:18] Lina: Yup, I'll share the compliance pack.
[02:20] Evan: One ops note — last week we saw a few 503s during a backfill run; root cause looked like autoscaler not picking up ephemeral load spikes. If we go dedicated, can we do better autoscaling?
[02:32] Samir: Dedicated has more deterministic capacity but you can still configure burst pools and auto-bump policies. We can set a buffer so short spikes don't cause request drops. For the backfill pattern, enabling pre-warming and a short-lived burst queue helped other customers.
[02:45] Dr. Maya Rios: What's the expected latency change if we enable batching more aggressively? Our clinicians are sensitive to response times.
[02:52] Samir: Batching reduces compute overhead but can add artificial latency waiting for batch windows. For Helion's median request size a 20-30ms batching window yields big token-cost wins while adding ~10-20ms p99 for short queries; but for longer generative flows the relative impact is smaller. We can tune per-route.
[03:11] Carlos: Can you show current cost distribution? Like which models and routes are the major drivers?
[03:17] Avery: We prepared an initial breakdown but I'll send a more detailed per-model per-route slice as an action item. Quick peek: the triage assistant and discharge summarizer are the top spenders.
[03:29] [03:30] Samir: Also worth noting, the embedding calls for search are cheap per call but they're frequent; caching embedding vectors locally for intra-session similarity dramatically reduced calls in a POC we ran.
[03:42] Dr. Maya Rios: On the roadmap front: we'd like to align on success criteria for the pilot. Finance needs a projected 30% reduction in variable cost or it's hard to justify a commit.
[03:53] Priya: Also, we have a hard egress rule: no outbound connections to unknown third parties from our VPC. So the pilot needs to be Private deployment or VPC peered Dedicated.
[04:04] Avery: That's fine. Samir - what's realistic to prove a 30% improvement in a one-week pilot?
[04:09] Samir: If we enable KV caching on the top two heavy routes, set batching for low-latency windows, and use a quantized model variant for short responses, we should see 25-40% reduction in per-token cost in synthetic runs. Real production will vary, but the pilot will capture real traffic.
[04:24] Evan: For the pilot, we need end-to-end observability. Will Redwood expose token-level breakdown and per-route latency at the granularity we can feed into our internal dashboards?
[04:33] Lina: Console provides token-level cost and per-route latency. We can give an export hook and a Prometheus endpoint for key metrics.
[04:40] Evan: Prometheus endpoint would be great. We can ingest and create incident thresholds.
[04:44] Carlos: A practical question on model variants — what does Redwood recommend for quantization level? We have some strict quality checks for summaries. If quantized models introduce hallucinations we can't ship.
[04:56] Samir: We usually recommend INT8 for short responses and INT4 for high-throughput non-critical paths. For summarization where fidelity is important, keep FP16 or lightly quantized INT8 and run regression tests against a prompt set. Redwood Optimize can run those evals and flag quality regressions.
[05:13] Dr. Maya Rios: We'll need Redwood Optimize results as part of the pilot acceptance criteria. Can you run those evals on our prompt set?
[05:20] Samir: Yes — if you share the prompt suite we can run Optimize and provide a delta table (latency, cost, rouge/bleu-like proxies).
[05:27] Priya: Is there any data residency issue with Optimize running in Redwood hosted infra?
[05:33] Lina: For sensitive datasets we offer an on-prem/Private run of Optimize or we can run it on a dedicated sandbox in your VPC. We'll include that in the compliance pack.
[05:42] Dr. Maya Rios: Ok. Regarding billing: if we do dedicated, is there an overage model? Finance wants guardrails.
[05:50] Avery: Dedicated has committed baseline and a burst pool with defined overage rates. We can model a monthly cap and alerting; also, rollbacks to hosted fallback are possible if dedicated gets saturated.
[05:59] Evan: About alerts — last month's spike triggered several false positives. We need better error classification. Can Redwood's tracing help pinpoint upstream app errors vs inference timeouts?
[06:09] Samir: Yes, request traces include routing, cache hits/misses, and kernel-level latency slices. We'll show an example trace after the call.
[06:17] Carlos: Can you share the previous incident trace? It might help us correlate with our backfill job.
[06:21] Lina: I'll attach the trace link to the follow-up notes.
[06:24] [06:26] Dr. Maya Rios: On governance: our security team requires KMS-managed keys inside our cloud account. Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
[06:33] Samir: Yep — we support CMK in AWS and equivalents in other clouds; encryption keys never leave your account for Private and Dedicated with VPC setup.
[06:42] Priya: Good. Also would like RBAC mapping — mapping of Redwood roles to our IAM.
[06:47] Lina: We'll include default RBAC templates and a mapping doc.
[06:50] [07:00] Avery: Let's talk timeline. If we kick off the pilot next week, what's the minimal setup tasks from Helion?
[07:06] Priya: Provide VPC peering details and a list of top routes we want cached. We'll need a small maintenance window for routing changes.
[07:13] Carlos: We'll also need the sample prompt sets and the acceptance criteria for summarization quality.
[07:19] Dr. Maya Rios: Finance will hold final sign off until they see a conservative projection. Can Avery include a conservative and optimistic case in the cost model?
[07:27] Avery: Absolutely. I will send both cases — conservative assumes only cache on one route and conservative batching; optimistic enables cache on two top routes and INT8 quantization.
[07:36] [07:40] Samir: One last technical note — for the backfill pattern you mentioned, pre-warming and a burst pool are the two knobs. If you have scheduled heavy jobs, we can make that explicit in autoscaler rules.
[07:50] Evan: We'll provide the backfill schedule.
[07:53] Priya: Also, if we're doing VPC peering we need a clear runbook for cutover. Can Redwood provide a dry-run checklist?
[07:59] Lina: Yes — we have a standard dry-run checklist. I'll add Helion-specific items and share.
[08:05] Dr. Maya Rios: Okay, sounds like solid plan. Let's recap next steps.
[08:09] Avery: Recap: Redwood to send cost breakdown (Avery), spin up dedicated pilot (Samir), compliance docs (Lina). Helion to provide VPC details, prompt sets, and backfill schedule (Priya/Carlos/Evan). We reconvene after pilot week to review metrics and decide on commit.
[08:26] Carlos: One quick nit — can you include an estimation of expected latency p95 change for each knob? That helps engineering communicate to clinicians.
[08:34] Samir: Yep, I'll include p50/p95/p99 deltas per knob.
[08:37] Dr. Maya Rios: Great. If no one has other items, we'll close. Thanks all.
[08:41] [END]
